pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/judge.rs:510 An exec dimension voided by a sandbox outage (the gate's own instrument hole) is excluded from both the overall and its floor. A case whose floor-1.0, weight-3 exec dimension never ran therefore passes on the remaining dimensions; the test at crates/engine/src/judge/tests/deterministic.rs:278 asserts exactly that.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/judge.rs:510 An instrument hole is resolved as SKIP, where the standard says FAIL-CLOSED (or REFUSE the case). Only the all-voided case is refused (judge.rs:520). The skip is at least rendered per dimension (ScoreDim.voided). Voiding a grounding dimension with zero claims is a subject-world absence, so SKIP is correct there.
crates/engine/src/judge.rs:473 Could-not-run, meaning no sample parsed, is returned as an error. It is never turned into a confident 0.0 fail.
crates/engine/src/judge.rs:555 Pass is built in code from the threshold and per-dimension floors. It is never taken from the model's own pass field.
crates/engine/src/fence.rs:9 The gated candidate writes the artifact the judge reads. Nonce fencing stops it from authoring the verdict, and an imitation attempt is flagged on the outcome.
crates/engine/src/scorers.rs:214 A misconfigured dimension is refused with the two fields the operator can actually set.

pairs.registryProposal: unmeasurable-criteria offers FAIL-CLOSED for a partial instrument hole beside the work. In a cross-candidate benchmark that scores the operator's sandbox outage as the candidate's failure and skews the comparison, which is why this code chose SKIP. The technique should name per-case REFUSE (no verdict for that case, counted in the run) as the resolution when the verdict feeds a comparison rather than a merge decision. Without it, implementers fall back to SKIP, and SKIP lets a floor-gated dimension pass unmeasured.
